title: NRI Home Loans: Down Payment vs. Overseas Savings Post-RBI Hike
description: Recent RBI rate hikes have increased floating interest rates on home loans, impacting Equated Monthly Instalments (EMIs) for Non-Resident Indians (NRIs). NRIs.

faq.q: How do RBI rate hikes specifically affect NRI home loans?
faq.a: RBI rate hikes increase the benchmark rates in India, which banks use to price home loans. For NRIs with floating rate loans, this means higher EMIs or extended loan tenures. For new loans, the initial interest rate will be higher.

faq.q: Is it always better to make a larger down payment?
faq.a: Not necessarily. While a larger down payment reduces interest costs and EMIs, it also reduces your liquidity. The decision depends on your emergency fund status, alternative investment opportunities, and risk appetite.

faq.q: What are the tax implications of using overseas savings for a down payment?
faq.a: Funds transferred from NRE (Non-Resident External) accounts to India for a down payment are generally tax-free in India. However, you should confirm any tax implications in your country of residence and consult a tax expert.

faq.q: Can I switch my floating rate loan to a fixed rate after a hike?
faq.a: Some banks offer the option to switch from a floating to a fixed rate loan, usually for a fee. However, fixed rates are typically higher than floating rates during a rising interest rate cycle, and the fixed period might be limited.

faq.q: How does currency fluctuation impact my decision?
faq.a: If you expect the Indian Rupee to depreciate significantly against your earning currency, retaining overseas savings might be beneficial as your EMIs would effectively become cheaper in foreign currency terms. Conversely, if the Rupee is expected to strengthen, a larger down payment now could be advantageous.

An NRE (Non-Resident External) account is a bank account opened in India by an NRI to deposit foreign earnings. The funds in an NRE account are freely repatriable, and the interest earned is tax-exempt in India.
